assessment: Assignment changes and renames suggest selection problems, but their causes are unproven. Two mechanism combinations merit bounded tests; neither establishes delivery within six engineer-days or achievement of the next-40-export targets.

openings.claim: Combine requested-week membership resolution with stable course identity at a center-scoped course-ID manifest interface, then render the documented CSV. Temporal resolution could preserve membership through instructor changes while identity resolution preserves it through renames.
openings.delta: Either component alone may leave the other source of omission intact; together they could preserve a course that is reassigned and renamed during one week.
openings.prediction: On fabricated combined-change fixtures, both components recover the intended course set while either alone fails. Ambiguous splits require an explicit mapping rather than automatic inclusion.
openings.probe: Compare baseline, temporal-only, identity-only, and combined selectors on unchanged, reassigned, renamed, combined-change, and split fixtures. Verify exact course membership, center ownership, CSV import, and concurrent attendance writes; estimate implementation and hosting cost before adoption.
assumptions: Stable course identities and sufficient week-specific assignment evidence exist or can be captured within the budget.
Read-only export preparation can coexist with attendance entry.

openings.claim: Combine coordinator course/week confirmation with immediate authorized regeneration at a validated center-week request interface inside the private service.
openings.delta: Confirmation alone still leaves replacement delays; regeneration alone can repeat the wrong selection. Passing confirmed scope into regeneration could make one correction produce a usable file.
openings.prediction: Compared with either component alone, the combination reduces repeated requests and active handling when the confirmed scope is accurate; stale timetables may erase this advantage.
openings.probe: Use counterbalanced fabricated tasks with six coordinators across two sessions. Separately time checking, correction, downloading, importing, and waiting; compare intended sets with task answers. Reject foreign-center course IDs server-side and test regeneration during attendance entry.
assumptions: A small internal confirmation surface and rerun control fit six engineer-days and existing hosting.
The existing CSV renderer can accept validated explicit scope.
